text: dsh-tool-index 是面向 DSH 的工具索引插件：它在 agent 创建和系统提示组装时接入工具注册流程，把符合前缀规则的 MCP 工具整理成按服务器分组的索引，并在工具达到阈值后延后提供完整定义。模型可先查工具名称、参数签名和摘要，再按需读取详细参数并调用原工具；名称输入不匹配时会提示相近名称。它适合连接了许多 MCP 服务、希望减少每轮提示中工具定义的 DSH 用户。默认无需额外密钥或账号。

dsh-tool-index indexes MCP tools in DSH and defers full definitions past a threshold. The model can inspect names and signatures, request parameters, then call the original tool. Close-name suggestions help with typos. It suits users with many MCP tools; no extra key or account is required.
希望 DSH 先只展示 MCP 工具目录，需要时再展开具体参数。
How can I keep many MCP tool schemas out of each prompt until they are needed?
dsh-tool-index 的功能「按需查看并调用 MCP 工具」：提示组装时将匹配的工具转为索引，模型可查询所选工具的完整说明和参数，再通过 call_tool 执行原工具。

dsh-tool-index README · dsh-tool-index：**75 MCP tools connected, one small task: 183,274 tokens without this plugin, 79,838 with it — 56% less.**

`dsh-tool-index` sends your MCP tool definitions as a compact index and loads full schemas only when the model asks for them. The tool list itself never changes mid-session, so your prompt cache keeps working.

A plugin for [DSH](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). Built on DeepSeek Harness; not an official DeepSeek project.

dsh-tool-index README · The problem：Every tool definition is sent again on every model request. Connect a few MCP servers and an agent carries hundreds of definitions it never uses: thousands of tokens on every step, and a model that picks tools worse because it has too many to choose from.

dsh-tool-index README · What it does：`dsh-tool-index` sends those tools as a short index instead: each tool's **name, parameters and one-line summary**, grouped by server. When the model needs one, it reads the full details with `tool_details` and runs it with `call_tool`.

```
without:  read, bash, mcp__github__create_issue {full schema}, mcp__github__list_issues {full schema}, ... ×180
with:     read, bash, tool_details {index: 180 names + one-liners}, call_tool
```

dsh-tool-index README · What it does：- **Fewer tokens on every request.** The MCP tools cost about 88% less per request.
- **The prompt cache keeps working.** The tool list stays the same for the whole session, so loading a tool never forces the provider to re-read the conversation at full price.
- **The model doesn't miss tools.** Every tool is always named in the index, and a wrong name (a typo, a missing `mcp__server__` prefix) gets the closest real names back.
- **Nothing is bypassed.** Permission policies, approvals and hooks still see the real tool and its arguments.

dsh-tool-index README · Does it save tokens?：Yes. One small task, three runs per cell, with real MCP servers:

| Model | Without the plugin | With it | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek deepseek-flash, 25 MCP tools | 80,777 | 58,864 | **-27%** |
| DeepSeek deepseek-flash, 75 MCP tools | 183,274 | 79,838 | **-56%** |
| Claude claude-haiku-5-5, 25 MCP tools | 110,598 | 94,422 | **-15%** |
| OpenAI gpt-5.4-mini, 25 MCP tools | 50,846 | 23,398 | **-54%** |

dsh-tool-index README · Does it save tokens?：And over a 5-message conversation in one session (DeepSeek, two of the messages need no tools):

| Servers | Without the plugin | With it | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 25 MCP tools | 159,736 | 106,398 | **-33%** |
| 75 MCP tools | 317,040 | 147,120 | **-54%** |

Tokens summed over every model step. Every run finished its task with and without the plugin. The more tools you connect, the more it saves.

Reproduce them yourself with `e2e/run.sh`.

dsh-tool-index README · Install：As a bundle in a profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile tui add dsh-tool-index
dsh --profile tui
```

Or from a checkout, for one run:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/GunjanPatel359/dsh-tool-index
cd dsh-tool-index
dsh tui --patch ./examples/local.patch.yml
```

dsh-tool-index README · Configuration：```yaml
- id: dsh-tool-index
  name: dsh-tool-index
  config:
    match: ['mcp__']          # MCP name prefixes to defer

A patch replaces a row's whole `config`, so restate every key you set.

With fewer than `minTools` matching tools nothing changes: a handful of definitions costs less than an extra step.

Keep tools the agent uses on most turns out of the index with `exclude` or `alwaysLoad`.

dsh-tool-index README · Configuration：This plugin is for MCP tools. `match` takes name prefixes, but deferring your harness's own core tools (`read`, `bash` and the like) will make the agent worse, not cheaper: it needs them on almost every turn, and there is no guard against it.

dsh-tool-index README · Trade-offs：- **Sometimes one extra step** (`tool_details`) before a deferred tool is first used in a conversation.
- **Arguments are checked by the tool, not by the provider.** A wrong argument comes back as the tool's own error.
- **UIs show `call_tool`** as the outer step, with the real tool inside it.

dsh-tool-index README · Compatibility：- **Native tool calls:** the mode the plugin is built for.
- **PTC mode** (`run_code`): the plugin steps aside for those agents and adds nothing to their requests. In PTC mode the model calls tools from code, and DSH already lists every tool for that code.
- **Sub-agents and structured-output children:** each agent gets its own index of its own tools. A child's `structured_output` tool stays a normal tool.
dsh-tool-index README · Compatibility：Written for DSH 0.2.x. DSH is pre-1.0, so its plugin interfaces can change between releases.
